title: Mid-esophageal mass in a smoker/drinker: squamous cell carcinoma (keratin pearls, intercellular bridges)
vignette: A 65-year-old man comes to the office with dysphagia. For the last 3 months, he has relied on protein shakes and juices for nourishment as he has had difficulty swallowing solid foods. He has also had a diminished appetite and an estimated weight loss of 9.1 kg (20 lb). Medical history includes hyperlipidemia, emphysema, and previous episodes of pancreatitis. Family history includes lung cancer in his mother. The patient smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 50 years but quit 2 years ago. He has been drinking a fifth (750 mL) of vodka weekly for the last decade. Vital signs are normal. BMI is 19.2 kg/m2. Temporal wasting is present but physical examination is otherwise unremarkable. Upper endoscopy reveals a 4-cm mass in the middle third of the esophagus, and several biopsies are taken. Thoracic imaging reveals mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Histologic evaluation of the biopsy specimens will most likely show which of the following in this patient?

clues.note: Progressive dysphagia to solids (then liquids) with weight loss suggests a mechanically obstructing esophageal malignancy.

clues.text: smoked a pack of cigarettes daily for 50 years
clues.note: Heavy tobacco use is a major risk factor for esophageal SQUAMOUS CELL carcinoma.

clues.text: drinking a fifth (750 mL) of vodka weekly
clues.note: Alcohol is a major risk factor for squamous cell carcinoma of the esophagus (synergistic with tobacco).

clues.text: 4-cm mass in the middle third of the esophagus
clues.note: Squamous cell carcinoma most often occurs in the proximal/MIDDLE third of the esophagus (adenocarcinoma favors the distal third).

whatMatters: A MID-esophageal mass with dysphagia/weight loss in a heavy SMOKER and DRINKER = esophageal SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA. Histology shows sheets of atypical squamous cells with KERATIN PEARLS and INTERCELLULAR BRIDGES. Answer C.
strategy: Localize (middle third), risk-stratify (tobacco + alcohol), and recall SCC histology: keratin pearls + intercellular bridges. Reject adenocarcinoma histology (irregular glandular, mucin-producing, invasive cells; distal esophagus, Barrett/GERD) - choices A (intestinal metaplasia without dysplasia = Barrett) and B (glandular invasion). Reject leiomyosarcoma (myocytes with atypia) and GI stromal tumor (spindle cells expressing CD117/c-KIT).

options.text: Irregular glandular cells with tissue invasion

eliminations.label: Intestinal cells without dysplasia - Barrett esophagus
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: nondysplastic intestinal metaplasia (Barrett esophagus). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Barrett is a premalignant change (from chronic GERD) in the DISTAL esophagus, not an invasive mid-esophageal cancer. ✅ Correct if: metaplastic columnar mucosa from reflux.

eliminations.label: Irregular glandular cells with invasion - adenocarcinoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: invasive glandular (mucin-producing) carcinoma = adenocarcinoma. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: adenocarcinoma arises in the DISTAL third from Barrett/GERD, whereas this smoking/alcohol-related MIDDLE-third tumor is squamous. ✅ Correct if: distal esophageal adenocarcinoma with Barrett.

eliminations.label: Myocytes with atypia - leiomyosarcoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: malignant smooth-muscle tumor (leiomyosarcoma). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is rare in the esophagus and shows atypical myocytes, not squamous features. ✅ Correct if: smooth-muscle malignancy.

eliminations.label: Spindle cells expressing CD117 - GIST
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: gastrointestinal stromal tumor (spindle cells, CD117/c-KIT positive). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: GISTs occur mainly in the stomach/small intestine and are rare in the esophagus; histology is spindled, not squamous. ✅ Correct if: CD117-positive stromal tumor (stomach).

reasoning: Progressive dysphagia + weight loss with a mid-esophageal mass = esophageal cancer
Heavy tobacco and alcohol use and the middle-third location point to squamous cell carcinoma
SCC histology shows keratin pearls and intercellular bridges
-> keratin pearls and intercellular bridges; answer C
mechanism: ESOPHAGEAL SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (SCC) arises from the squamous epithelium lining the PROXIMAL and MIDDLE thirds of the esophagus (most common in the MIDDLE third). Major risk factors are TOBACCO and ALCOHOL (synergistic), plus hot beverages, nitrosamine-containing foods, achalasia, and caustic strictures. It presents with progressive DYSPHAGIA (solids then liquids), weight loss, and often mediastinal lymphadenopathy (lymphatics of the upper/middle esophagus drain to mediastinal nodes). Histology shows nests/sheets of atypical SQUAMOUS cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, KERATIN PEARLS (concentric keratinized whorls), and INTERCELLULAR BRIDGES (desmosomal connections). This contrasts with esophageal ADENOCARCINOMA, which arises in the DISTAL third from Barrett esophagus/chronic GERD and shows mucin-producing glandular cells. The remaining distractors are Barrett metaplasia (nondysplastic intestinal cells), leiomyosarcoma (atypical myocytes), and GI stromal tumor (CD117-positive spindle cells) - not features of esophageal SCC.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid GI/Path > esophageal SCC: proximal/middle third; risk = tobacco, alcohol, hot liquids, nitrosamines, achalasia; keratin pearls + intercellular bridges; mediastinal nodes; vs adenocarcinoma (distal, Barrett/GERD).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Middle-third mass + smoking/alcohol = squamous cell carcinoma (keratin pearls, intercellular bridges).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on squamous vs adenocarcinoma, keratin pearls, intercellular bridges, Barrett esophagus, or dysphagia progression? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Glandular/mucin/Barrett = adenocarcinoma (distal); myocytes = leiomyosarcoma; CD117 spindle = GIST.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: esophageal SCC = middle third + tobacco/alcohol; keratin pearls + intercellular bridges; adenocarcinoma = distal/Barrett.

firstAid.detail: Path: keratin pearls + intercellular bridges; middle third; tobacco/alcohol.

memoryHook: Smoke + booze scarring the MIDDLE of the swallowing tube -> squamous cancer, and squamous cells leave 'pearls' of keratin joined by tiny bridges.
